title: Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed Honours Kenya's National Heroes
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Nairobi, Kenya -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed paid tribute to Kenya's freedom fighters and national heroes during Mashujaa Day celebrations in Eldoret on Tuesday, highlighting the two countries' shared history of struggle, sacrifice and national unity.

title: Who Protects the Protectors? Inside the Growing Danger for Ethiopia's Humanitarian Workers
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- When humanitarian workers travel to the field, they carry more than food, medicine, or information. They carry the hopes of people facing hunger, displacement, illness, and conflict. Yet, the danger increasingly exposes those delivering this assistance.

title: Obituary - Prominent Kenyan Oromo Scholar, Anthropologist Professor Abdullahi Shongolo Passes Away
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Professor Abdullahi Shongolo, a prominent scholar of history and anthropology whose research on Borana Oromo culture, customary law, and history brought international attention to the community's rich heritage, passed away on 20 October at the age of 68 at Nanyuki Hospital in Kenya, following an illness from which he did not recover.

title: Entrenched Authoritarianism: Ethiopia's Rule of Law Index Slides Further
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's rule of law performance has deteriorated further, with the country ranking 133rd out of 143 countries and jurisdictions in the 2026 World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index, according to the ranking provided for this report. The latest assessment extends a multi-year decline that has seen the country remain near the bottom of global and sub-Saharan African comparisons.

title: Supreme Audit Institutions Deliberating On Strengthening Collaboration, Accountability in Africa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- A workshop aimed at strengthening collaboration and improving the effectiveness and sustainability of public-sector auditing across Africa is underway in Addis Ababa.

title: TPLF Had Been Preparing for War - PM Abiy
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The defunct TPLF had been preparing for another round of war, violating the Pretoria Agreement, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed revealed.

title: PM Abiy Honors Kenya's Heroes, Highlights Shared Legacy of Unity
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has paid tribute to Kenya's freedom fighters and national heroes during the Mashujaa Day celebrations in Eldoret, Kenya.

title: Ethiopia Calls for Data-Driven Policymaking to Accelerate Africa's Progress
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has reformed its statistical legislation and established an independent statistical service to strengthen the production and coordination of official data, President Taye Atske Selassie said.

title: PM Abiy Reviews Ethiopia's Progress Toward Nuclear Energy Development
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has visited the Ethiopian Nuclear Energy Commission to review progress in developing the country's nuclear energy program.

title: News - Funding Shortfalls Threaten Health Services in Ethiopia's Conflict-Hit Regions, UN Warns
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Funding shortages threaten essential health and nutrition services in Ethiopia's conflict-affected regions, with 10 of the 16 operational mobile health and nutrition teams in Amhara expected to shut down by the end of October, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said.

title: Eritrea Tells Us There Is No 'Crisis' Between Ethiopia and Eritrea
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Eritrea's Ambassador to the United Nations, Sophia Tesfamariam, has told senior US diplomats that there is no "crisis" between Ethiopia and Eritrea, while urging Washington and other international actors to address what she described as threats to Eritrea's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

title: Ethiopia's Sovereign Access to Seaport Crucial for Regional Shared Prosperity - Scholars
summary: [ENA] Scholars have noted that Ethiopia's sovereign access to seaport plays a crucial role in ensuring regional shared prosperity.

title: Prisoner of History, Not Geography

Addis Abeba told council members that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, which Eritrea denies. Asmara replied by calling the accusation a declaration of war and asking the council to take deterrent measures. title: News - 13-Year-Old Girl Killed After Flag Dispute in Borana's Moyale - Protesters Block Transport Services
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The opening of a new Somali Region administration office and the raising of its flag in Moyale town in Borana zone of Oromia regional state on October 18 triggered an exchange of gunfire between Somali regional forces and Oromia local militias, leaving a 13-year-old girl dead and prompting protests that disrupted transport services and forced businesses to close on Monday, residents told Addis Standard.

title: PM Abiy Says Eritrean People Have Lost Former Assets Since Secession
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said Eritrean people have lost much of its industrial capacity and urban vitality since secession, urging good neighborliness and development cooperation as the path forward.

title: Ethiopia Signs Second-Phase LNG Development Deal for Ogaden Gas Field
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Chinese companies GCL Group and Jurong Group have signed an agreement to develop the second phase of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) project at Ethiopia's Calub gas field in the Somali Region, as the government seeks to expand commercial use of the country's natural gas reserves.

title: PM Abiy Warns Eritrea of 'Extremely Severe' Consequences If It Rejects Peace Call
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has warned Eritrea of "extremely severe" consequences if its government continues to reject Ethiopia's calls for peace and regional cooperation, accusing Asmara of aligning itself with forces seeking to destabilize Ethiopia. He also called on Tigrayan youth to abandon armed struggle, accusing Tigrayan People's Liberation Front (TPLF) leaders of prolonging conflict at the expense of the region's population.

title: Ethiopia's Abiy Urges Investment in Youth As Kenya Honors National Heroes
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has called for greater investment in young people, saying Kenya's next phase of development will depend on its ability to turn freedom into economic opportunities for the next generation.

title: Somalia's Aid Paradox - Saving Lives, Sustaining Dependency
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- For more than three decades, international aid has been an indispensable lifeline for Somalia. It has helped prevent humanitarian collapse, funded essential health and education services, and sustained civil-society organizations through cycles of conflict, drought, and displacement. title: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Mekelle, the capital of Tigray Regional State, has now changed hands three times in six years. Federal forces took the city in November 2020, within a month of the last war beginning; Tigrayan forces retook it in June 2021. On 3 October 2026, federal troops and the allied Tigray Peace Force entered it again, after the TPLF announced that it had withdrawn and that its regional administration would "temporarily move out" of the capital. title: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has warned that recognizing Somaliland could undermine regional counterterrorism efforts and strengthen Al-Shabaab, while Somaliland officials have rejected the security concerns, arguing that recognition would instead enhance regional stability and advance Ethiopia's economic and strategic interests.

title: Oromo Intellectuals Back Ola-Fano Membership in New Armed Alliance, Call for Inclusive Transition in Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A group of Oromo intellectuals and public figures has backed the Oromo Liberation Army's (OLA) participation in a newly formed opposition coalition that includes the Amhara Fano movement, describing the alliance as a potential opening to address Ethiopia's deepening political crisis while calling for an inclusive transition that safeguards the rights and political aspirations of all communities.

title: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Airbus has forecast a sixfold rise in Ethiopia's air passenger traffic over the next 20 years, saying Ethiopian Airlines is well placed to turn Addis Ababa into one of Africa's leading aviation hubs.

title: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October.

title: Alliance for Survival Rejects Rubio's Characterization of Ethiopia's Conflict As Separatist, Terrorist
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival (Alliance for Survival), a coalition of armed and political groups opposing the federal government, has rejected remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterizing aspects of Ethiopia's conflict as separatist and terrorist, calling on Washington to adopt what it described as a balanced approach to the conflict.

title: Ugandans in Ethiopia Called to Contribute to Country's Growth Through Investment, Trade and Skills Transfer
summary: [Independent (Kampala)] Addis Ababa -- Uganda convened its diaspora community in Ethiopia for a two-day event at the Hilton Addis Ababa, centered on "Connecting, Celebrating and Contributing: Harnessing the Ugandan Diaspora for National Development." The forum aimed to strengthen ties between Ugandans living in Ethiopia and national development priorities, while showcasing Uganda's culture, investment opportunities, and talent to a global audience.

title: Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Ethiopian high-level delegation met with Eric Meyer, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Africa and the Middle East at the U.S. Department of the Treasury, on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

title: African Diplomats Urge Stronger African-Led Strategies, Sustained Dialogue, Local Ownership, Adequate Financing
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- African diplomats have called for stronger African-led strategies to address the continent's conflicts and security challenges.

title: Why Ethiopia's Return to Red Sea Is Indispensable Asset for Regional Peace and Stability?
summary: [ENA] Ethiopia has a long history of contributing to regional, continental and international peacekeeping missions, guided by its commitment to collective security, Pan-Africanism and regional stability. Its pursuit of reliable maritime access presents an opportunity to expand this role by contributing to maritime security, protecting international trade and promoting lasting peace across the Red Sea region.
